cues: Phrasal verbs are learnt with their meaning.
Run out of: have none left.
Most can be split: turn the offer down, or turn down the offer.
With a pronoun the split is compulsory: turn it down, never turn down it.
And verbs with two particles, like put up with, are never split.
text: Phrasal verbs are learnt with their meaning. Put up with: tolerate. Put off: postpone. Call off: cancel. Look into: investigate. Bring up: raise. Turn down: reject. Carry out: perform. Run out of: have none left. Most can be split: turn the offer down, or turn down the offer. With a pronoun the split is compulsory: turn it down, never turn down it. And verbs with two particles, like put up with, are never split.
